/tools/image-compressor.title: Image Compressor - Compress JPG, PNG, WebP in Your Browser
/tools/image-compressor.description: Compress images without uploading. Works on JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF. Free, no signup, no tracking. Files stay on your device.

@graph.name: Image Compressor
@graph.description: Free browser-based image compressor for JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF. Files never leave your device.
@graph.browserRequirements: Requires a modern browser with Canvas support.
featureList: Compress JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF images
Files processed locally in the browser

mainEntity.name: Is my image sent to a server?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The file is read into browser memory and compressed by code running locally in your browser. The file is not transmitted to a server for processing.

mainEntity.name: What file size can I compress?

acceptedAnswer.text: Up to 25 MB per image. This limit is enforced before processing to protect browser memory.

mainEntity.name: Which image formats are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: Input: JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF. Output: JPEG, WebP and PNG. GIF animations are not preserved; only a single frame is output.

mainEntity.name: Does compression reduce image quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: JPEG and WebP use lossy compression, so some quality is lost at lower settings. PNG output is lossless. Adjust the quality slider to balance size against visual quality.

mainEntity.name: Does this tool work without internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: After the first load, some parts of the tool may continue to work because the browser has cached the page. However, this site does not currently include a service worker, so it is not guaranteed to work offline.

mainEntity.name: Can I compress multiple images at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Add multiple files; each is processed independently and can be downloaded individually or together.

mainEntity.name: Is there a watermark or signup?

acceptedAnswer.text: No watermark and no signup. The tool is free to use and does not require an account.

mainEntity.name: Why is my PNG larger after compression?

acceptedAnswer.text: PNG is lossless. Re-encoding may occasionally increase file size. Choose WebP or JPEG output for a smaller file when transparency is not required.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between JPEG and WebP?

acceptedAnswer.text: WebP typically produces smaller files at similar visual quality and supports transparency. JPEG is more widely supported by older software and does not support transparency.

mainEntity.name: Does compressing the same image twice reduce quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for lossy formats. Each re-encode of a JPEG or WebP image loses some quality. Start from the original file whenever possible.

mainEntity.name: Is my image sent to a server?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The file is read into browser memory and resized by code running locally in your browser. The file is not transmitted to a server for processing.

mainEntity.name: What file size can I resize?

acceptedAnswer.text: Up to 25 MB per image. This limit is enforced before processing to protect browser memory.

mainEntity.name: Which image formats are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: Input: JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF. Output: JPEG, WebP and PNG. GIF animations are not preserved; only a single frame is output.

mainEntity.name: Will resizing reduce image quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Downscaling discards information, so the result will have fewer pixels. Upscaling cannot add detail. Choose the exact size you need and keep the original file.

mainEntity.name: Can I maintain the aspect ratio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. When only one dimension is set, the other is calculated from the original aspect ratio. You can also enter both dimensions to stretch the image.
